Your suspicion levels above are your own accumulated evidence from the whole game — trust them over meeting rhetoric. A suspect two independent witnesses place at the scene, or whose account one of the conflicts above contradicts, is a stronger case than one carried by a single voice. Remember the vent mechanic: an impostor vents BETWEEN rooms invisibly, so your own sightings of someone leaving or being elsewhere earlier do NOT clear them of a witnessed vent. The numbers on this page are for your decision, not for your mouth: never quote a suspicion score or any other bookkeeping figure in "rationale_text" — say what you saw.

- Fill at least one of the two reason ids on every EJECT; a SKIP needs neither.
- "considered_alternatives" lists at most two or three other players you weighed (empty if none).
- "rationale_text" is ONE short sentence (~20 words) IN YOUR OWN VOICE: say what actually convinced you, pointing at the evidence you cited, the way you would say it at the table. Half the table opens with the stock formula "p-N's alibi contradicts multiple sightings ..." — don't. Memory-citing — "My own log decides it: I watched that MEDBAY vent myself, and nothing said tonight outweighs it." Keep the whole object compact: a long rationale can overrun the output limit and truncate the JSON, which discards your vote.
</output_format>

## How to decide
Your maximum suspicion among the living ejection targets is **1.00**.

Your suspicion levels above are your own accumulated evidence from the whole game — trust them over meeting rhetoric. A suspect two independent witnesses place at the scene, or whose account one of the conflicts above contradicts, is a stronger case than one carried by a single voice. Remember the vent mechanic: an impostor vents BETWEEN rooms invisibly, so your own sightings of someone leaving or being elsewhere earlier do NOT clear them of a witnessed vent. If your strongest suspicion points at a row tagged OUT OF THE GAME, that case is already closed — the dead cannot be voted, so weigh only the LIVING targets and SKIP if none of them carries the case on its own. Every EJECT names its evidence: the transcript turn that convinced you (in "primary_reason_id"), or the [obs ...] memory line that did (in "primary_reason_observation_id") — a call you cannot source either way is a call to SKIP, and a SKIP needs no citation. Set "confidence" to your honest probability that the call is right, judged against the evidence you cite — a case you can barely source deserves a low number, and a case you cannot source at all deserves a SKIP. The numbers on this page are for your decision, not for your mouth: never quote a suspicion score or any other bookkeeping figure in "rationale_text" — say what you saw.

Keep the whole object compact: a long rationale can overrun the output limit and truncate the JSON, which discards your vote.

One exception, and only one: if the player you saw vent is already dead or ejected, that case is closed — say nothing about it and spend your turn on someone still in the game.
